signature.name: Jatiyo Sangsad Bhaban
signature.detail: Louis Kahn's monumental parliament complex is Dhaka's defining modern landmark and one of the most striking buildings in South Asia. It is a working government site, so access to the interior is limited; view it from the surrounding grounds and check locally whether visitor entry is open before you go.

signature.name: Lalbagh Fort
signature.detail: A 17th-century Mughal fort complex with gardens, a mosque and the tomb of Pari Bibi, and the most atmospheric historic site in the old city. Go in the cooler morning hours and dress modestly, as it is a heritage and religious-adjacent site.

signature.name: Ahsan Manzil
signature.detail: The pink riverside palace of the Nawabs is Dhaka's most photographed heritage building, now a museum of period rooms. It sits near Sadarghat, so combine it with a walk along the Buriganga; mornings are cooler and less crowded.

signature.name: Shaheed Minar
signature.detail: The iconic monument to the language movement martyrs and a symbol of Bengali identity, central to any understanding of the city. It is an open public memorial, free to visit; go early morning or evening and dress respectfully.

signature.name: Dhakeshwari Temple
signature.detail: Dhaka's principal Hindu temple and an important site of worship in the old city. Remove shoes before entering, dress modestly, and avoid photographing worshippers without permission.

transport: Rickshaw or CNG short hop under $2; rideshare and taxis cheap
